content: Nabidh was an intoxicating beverage. Abu Hurayrah narrated that he was aware the Apostle of Allah (peace be upon him) used to fast regularly. On a day when the Prophet was not fasting, Abu Hurayrah prepared a drink (nabidh) in a pumpkin and brought it to him. However, by the time it was presented, the drink had fermented. The Prophet instructed him to throw it against the wall, stating, This is a drink of those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day. When Umar was on his deathbed, his condition worsened due to the severity of his wound. His physician asked him which type of alcohol he would prefer to drink. Umar responded that his preferred choice was a drink called nabidh. Subsequently, this drink was administered to him. Yahya narrated to me from Malik, who narrated from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who narrated from Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, that Aslam, the freed slave of Umar ibn al-Khattab, informed him of an incident. Aslam had visited Abdullah ibn Ayyash al-Makhzumi and noticed that he had some nabidh with him while he was on his way to Makkah. Aslam remarked to him, Umar ibn al-Khattab loves this drink. Abdullah ibn Ayyash then carried a large drinking bowl filled with nabidh and brought it to Umar ibn al-Khattab, placing it before him. Umar brought the drink close to himself, raised his head, and remarked, This drink is good. He drank some of it and then passed it to the man on his right.
